text:
The Nifty 50 closed at 25,349.65, down 1.75% on the day, while the broader Nifty 500 fell 1.41%. The sell‑off was wide‑ranging – 133 stocks advanced against 360 declines, giving a breadth score of 62.2 (a “healthy” market but clearly bearish). Both major indices are trading below their 20‑day (63.4% of stocks) and 50‑day (55.9%) moving averages, and just under half of the Nifty 500 remain above the 200‑day average, indicating weakening momentum.

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) were net buyers, adding ₹5,672.99 cr today and a cumulative ₹33,454.98 cr over the past five sessions, while Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) sold ₹2,760.12 cr. FIIs have been buying for 18 straight days, whereas DIIs have been net sellers for four days. The options market shows a put‑call ratio (PCR) of 0.74 for Nifty and 0.71 for Bank Nifty, suggesting a slight bias toward call buying. Max‑pain levels sit at 25,350 for Nifty and 62,500 for Bank Nifty, with support walls around 25,300–25,400 and 62,500–62,600 respectively.

Watch the 25,562 P (pivot) and the S1 level of 25,131 on Nifty; a break below S1 could open further downside. For Bank Nifty, the pivot at 63,441 and S1 at 61,690 are key. Keep an eye on the India VIX, now at 17.7 (up 2.19%), and global cues such as oil price moves and US data, which may influence the next session’s direction.
